steps.title: Spanish table
steps.body: Tempranillo suits roast lamb, especially Castilian lechazo, suckling lamb, a classic with Ribera. Rioja goes with grilled lamb chops over vine cuttings, chorizo, jamón ibérico and Manchego cheese. Aged Gran Reserva suits mushrooms and game. Joven suits tapas.

steps.title: Service and age
steps.body: Serve at 16 to 18 degrees. Joven within two years; Crianza within five; Reserva five to fifteen; Gran Reserva 15 to 30 years or more. Old Rioja can throw sediment; decant gently. Ribera's big young wines benefit from air.

steps.prompt: Which Castilian dish is a classic with Ribera del Duero?
steps.explanation: Roast suckling lamb in wood ovens is Ribera's traditional match.

steps.body: A Rioja Reserva with jamón ibérico is a simple, classic Spanish pairing. The ham's fat and salt soften the wine's tannin.

steps.explanation: Sorbet is too sweet and acidic for a red.

points: Tempranillo suits lamb, jamón and Manchego
